original_question: Let a(n) be an integer sequence such that the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a(n)) converge for every basic generalized 2-step nilsequence ψ. Must it follow that for every system (X, X, µ, T, S) and f, g ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{a(n)} f · S^{a(n)} g converge weakly in L2(µ)?
target_in_paper: Section 4.2, Special Case of Problem 3 (immediately after Problem 3, in the subsection on necessary and sufficient conditions for ℓ-convergence).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s intended special case: it uses a single integer sequence a(n); the hypothesis is convergence of Cesàro averages against every basic generalized 2-step nilsequence; the conclusion is weak convergence in L^2(μ) of the bilinear averages; and it is set in the commuting-transformations framework rather than the older single-transformation/powers-of-the-same-transformation formulation.
missing_details: State explicitly that a: N -> Z is a sequence of integers and that all averages are Cesàro averages as N -> infinity.
Specify what a 'system' means here: a probability space (Y, 𝒴, μ) together with commuting, invertible, measure-preserving transformations T, S : Y -> Y.
Specify that f and g are bounded measurable functions, i.e. f, g in L^∞(μ).

Define 'basic generalized 2-step nilsequence' in the paper’s sense: a one-variable sequence ψ(n) = F(b^n x), where X = G/Γ is a 2-step nilmanifold, b is in G, x is in X, and F is Riemann-integrable on X; the word 'generalized' refers to allowing F to be Riemann-integrable instead of continuous.
Make clear that the conclusion is weak convergence in the weak topology of L^2(μ), not norm convergence in L^2(μ) and not pointwise convergence.
Indicate that this is the singled-out special case of the broader Problem 3, which in full concerns equivalence between nilsequence tests and ℓ-convergence for commuting transformations.
Do not add extra assumptions such as monotonicity of a(n) or positive density of its range; those are mentioned only as known cases, not as hypotheses of the open problem.
If you want the question to be fully stand-alone, avoid reusing X both for the probability space and for the nilmanifold.
refined_question: Let a : N -> Z be a sequence of integers such that, for every basic generalized 2-step nilsequence ψ(n) = F(b^n x), where X = G/Γ is a 2-step nilmanifold, b ∈ G, x ∈ X, and F is Riemann-integrable on X, the Cesàro averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a(n)) converge as N -> infinity. Must it then follow that for every probability space (Y, 𝒴, μ), every pair of commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations T, S : Y -> Y, and every f, g ∈ L^∞(μ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{a(n)}f · S^{a(n)}g converge weakly in L^2(μ) as N -> infinity?
justification: This is the paper’s exact singled-out open problem nearest to your draft: not the full Problem 3, and not the weighted variant that follows it, but the special case obtained by taking one integer sequence and asking whether nilsequence-test convergence forces weak L^2 convergence of the corresponding bilinear averages for two commuting transformations. The nearby context in Sections 1.2 and 2.4.2 supplies the hidden assumptions and notation needed to make the question self-contained.
